payload.name: Anchoring and adjustment
payload.fact: The anchoring and adjustment heuristic describes a process where individuals make initial judgments based on an anchor and then adjust from that point, often serving as a fundamental mechanism for inferential work.

provenance.title: Inferential Correction
provenance.quote_or_locus: anchoring and adjustment – describes the process by which the human mind does virtually all of its inferential work. Indeed, one of psychology's fundamental insights is that judgments are generally the products of nonconscious systems that operate quickly, on the basis of scant evidence, and in a routine manner, and then pass their hurried approximations to consciousness, which slowly and deliberately adjusts them
